(21 March 2015){{cite web|title=KCB - Nakuru AllStars (21/03-2015 14:00)|url=http://www.futaa.com//football/event/1939136|publisher=Futaa.com|date=21 March 2015|access-date=26 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150421061628/http://www.futaa.com//football/event/1939136|archive-date=21 April 2015|url-status=dead}} | prevseason = [[2014 Kenyan Premier League|2014]] | nextseason = [[2016 Kenyan Premier League|2016]] | extra information = | updated = 1 November 2015 }} The '''2015 Kenyan Premier League''' (known as the '''[[Tusker (African beer)|Tusker]] Premier League''' and thereafter the '''[[SportPesa]] Premier League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the twelfth season of the [[Kenyan Premier League]] since it began in 2003, and the 52nd season of top-division [[football in Kenya]] since 1963. It began on 21 February and ended on 1 November. Before the beginning of the season, talks with the [[Football Kenya Federation]] (FKF) concerning the expansion of the top tier to 18 teams fell through. While the KPL continued with its agenda for the season, the FKF created a parallel top division called the FKF Premier League (FKF PL), consisting of 18 teams. In March, an agreement was reached to maintain, for the 2015 season, the KPL as the top division with the FKF PL as the second tier. A total of 16 teams competed for the Kenyan Premier League, all returning from the [[2014 Kenyan Premier League|2014 season]]. [[Nairobi City Stars]] and [[Nakuru Top Fry AllStars|Top Fry AllStars]] were not replaced as membership for the FKF Premier League was drawn from majority of the teams from the [[2014 Kenyan National Super League]], including those that were to be promoted to the Kenyan Premier League. On 16 September, defending champions [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]] beat [[Sony Sugar F.C.|Sony Sugar]] 1–0 to win a third consecutive league title with 4 matches to spare.{{cite web |title=Wafula goal hands Gor the title |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/wafula-goal-hands-gor-the-title |date=16 September 2015 |author=Kevin Teya |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=20 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150918002552/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/wafula-goal-hands-gor-the-title |archive-date=18 September 2015 |url-status=dead }} Finishing the season unbeaten with a record of 24–6–0 (24 wins, 6 draws, no losses), Gor Mahia remained the only club in Kenya to complete an [[Perfect season|unbeaten season]] (after achieving the same feat in the [[1976 Kenya National Football League|1976 season]]) and became the only club in Kenya to have done so twice.{{cite web|title=Unbeaten Gor Mahia aim at achieving the success of 1976 |url=http://www.nation.co.ke/sports/football/Gor-Mahia-Kenyan-Premier-League-1976/-/1102/2744792/-/102w6nfz/-/index.html |author=Isaac Swila |work=[[Daily Nation]] |date=8 June 2015 |access-date=13 June 2015}} They also became the first club in Africa to finish a whole season unbeaten since [[Egyptian Premier League]] giants [[Al Ahly SC|Al Ahly]] went through both the [[2004–05 Egyptian Premier League|2004–05]] and [[2005–06 Egyptian Premier League|2005–06]] seasons without a single loss en route to their 30th and 31st league titles.{{cite web|title=Ahly surrender unbeaten record in Egypt |url=https://www.fifa.com/world-match-centre/news/newsid/109/374/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150615071719/http://www.fifa.com/world-match-centre/news/newsid/109/374/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 15, 2015 |work=[[Agence France-Presse|AFP]] |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=8 January 2007 |access-date=13 June 2015}} Gor Mahia will represent Kenya in the preliminary round of the [[2016 CAF Champions League]] and will play against the [[2015 FKF President's Cup]] champions at the [[2016 Kenyan Super Cup]]. ==Teams== {{location map+ |Kenya |float=right |width=380 |caption=Locations of the 2015 Kenyan Premier League £1.28 million [[Pound sterling|sterling]]; [[Euro|€]]1.62 million) with [[East African Breweries]] to rename the league to the [[Tusker (African beer)|Tusker]] Premier League (TPL).{{cite web |url=http://www.capitalfm.co.ke/sports/2012/08/21/kpl-now-tusker-pl-in-sh170m-deal/ |title=KPL now Tusker PL in Sh170m deal |publisher=[[98.4 Capital FM]] |date=21 August 2012 |access-date=21 August 2012}} For sponsorship reasons, the league was known by that name until 6 August 2015, when East African betting company SportPesa gained the naming rights to the league in a four-and-a-half-year deal reportedly worth KSh.450 million/= (approx. US$4.36 million, £2.84 million stg. or €3.87 million) to rename the league to the SportPesa Premier League,{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en-ke/news/4523/kenya-premier-league/2015/08/06/14201732/sportpesa-are-new-sponsors-of-kenyan-premier-league |title=SportPesa are new sponsors of Kenyan Premier League |date=6 August 2015 |publisher=Goal.com |access-date=9 October 2015}} nearly three times the value of the previous deal with Tusker. ==Pre-season crisis== {{Main|2015 in Kenyan football#Kenyan Premier League crisis}} Towards the end of the [[2014 in Kenyan football|2014 season]], the FKF proposed that the Premier League should be expanded to 18 teams from 16 for the upcoming season, though KPL management insisted that the 2015 season would continue with 16 teams.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-gags-debate-on-18-team-league |title=FKF gags debate on 18-team league |date=28 November 2014 |author=Kevin Teya |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231173437/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-gags-debate-on-18-team-league |archive-date=31 December 2014 |url-status=dead }} Reasons given by the KPL for the opposition of the expansion of the league included the [[Kenya national football team|national team]] needing more time for friendlies and competitive matches to increase the nation's [[FIFA World Rankings|FIFA World Ranking]], as well as an increased risk of injury to Premier League players – especially since only very few clubs have medical insurance to cover costs of the rehabilitation of players – further undermining the performance of the national team.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-says-no-to-18-team-league |title=KPL says no to 18-team league |date=25 November 2014 |author=Kevin Teya |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221122339/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-says-no-to-18-team-league |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} However, in a statement released on 25 November 2014, the FKF insisted that the decision to expand the league was "final and irreversible".{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-decision-on-18--team-kpl-is-final-and-irreversible |title=FKF: Decision on 18 - Team KPL is 'final and irreversible' |date=25 November 2014 |author=Kevin Teya |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141128045019/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-decision-on-18--team-kpl-is-final-and-irreversible |archive-date=28 November 2014 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }} On 19 December 2014, a statement signed by FKF chairman [[Sam Nyamweya]] and KPL chairman [[Ambrose Rachier]] revealed the formation of a six-man committee with three representatives from each side to hold talks with three [[FIFA]] delegates to come up with resolutions on the crisis.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-fkf-pick-joint-committee-to-sit-with-fifa |title=KPL, FKF pick joint committee to sit with FIFA |date=19 December 2014 |author=Wilson Mathu |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221123859/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-fkf-pick-joint-committee-to-sit-with-fifa |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} On 15 January 2015, Nyamweya announced that the 2015 Kenyan Premier League season was set to kick off on the second week of February, adding that the FKF was "working hard to ensure all matters are settled as soon as possible".{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-confirms-league-kick-off-date |title=FKF confirms league kick off date |date=15 January 2015 |author=Wilson Mathu |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221122354/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-confirms-league-kick-off-date |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} However, [[Cabinet of Kenya|Cabinet Secretary]] for [[Ministry of Sports, Culture and the Arts|Sports, Culture and the Arts]] [[Hassan Wario]] threatened to disband the FKF the next day, who he said were "letting down Kenya and the youths of this country."{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/cs-wario-blasts-fkf-threatens-to-disband-it |title=CS Wario blasts FKF; threatens to disband it |date=17 January 2015 |author=Wilson Mathu |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221124646/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/cs-wario-blasts-fkf-threatens-to-disband-it |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} On 27 January, the FKF ejected a consultant report sent in by FIFA delegate Robert Niemann regarding the Premier League after FIFA had directed that the report be released to all concerned parties in the crisis, including the KPL.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fifa-directs-fkf-to-release-report |title=FIFA directs FKF to release report |date=27 January 2015 |author=Kevin Teya |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221122652/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fifa-directs-fkf-to-release-report |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-rejects-fifa-report |title=FKF rejects FIFA report |date=27 January 2015 |author=Wilson Mathu |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221123617/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-rejects-fifa-report |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} Following a KPL Governing Council meeting held on 24 January 2015, the KPL announced four days later that the league was set to begin on 21 February with 16 teams, with fixtures to be reviewed and approved at a meeting to be held in early February. Committee members expressed hope that an agreement with the FKF would be finalised and signed before the league's kick-off, but authorised matches to be played with or without a signed agreement with the FKF.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-sets-2015-league-kick-off-date |title=KPL sets 2015 league kick off date |date=28 January 2015 |author=Mercy Njueh |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221052131/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-sets-2015-league-kick-off-date |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} In response, the FKF announced the creation of the FKF Premier League consisting of 18 teams just hours later, setting its kick-off date for 14 February.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-hits-back-creates-legitimate-league |title=FKF hits back, creates 'legitimate' league |date=28 January 2015 |author=Mercy Njueh |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221011001/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-hits-back-creates-legitimate-league |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} Top referees in Kenya showed their support for the KPL thereafter, with one referee asking that if the Federation "cannot be honest with such a small tournament [the [[2014 FKF President's Cup]]; officials had not yet been paid for their duties there], how can they be trusted to run the league?"{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/top-referees-back-kpl-blasts-fkf-over-unpaid-dues |title=Top referees back KPL, blasts FKF over unpaid dues |date=28 January 2015 |author=Mercy Njueh |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221123624/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/top-referees-back-kpl-blasts-fkf-over-unpaid-dues |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} On 30 January, Wario ordered the FKF to release the previously ejected FIFA report to all concerned parties including the Ministry of Sports, Culture and the Arts "without any further delay". In response, the FKF insisted that the report was not meant for "any other parties" other than itself and the Kenyan Premier League.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/government-orders-fkf-to-release-fifa-report |title=Government orders FKF to release FIFA report |date=30 January 2015 |author=Kevin Teya |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221124245/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/government-orders-fkf-to-release-fifa-report |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fifa-report-fkf-tells-off-gvt-et-al |title=FIFA report: FKF tells off Gvt et al |date=31 January 2015 |author=Wilson Mathu |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221123849/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fifa-report-fkf-tells-off-gvt-et-al |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} In a Special General Meeting convened by the FKF the same day, the governing body resolved to maintain its previous directive to stage the eighteen-team FKF Premier League.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-sgm-resolutions |title=FKF SGM: Resolutions |date=30 January 2015 |author=Sumba Bwire |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221124113/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-sgm-resolutions |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} On 2 February 2015, the KPL declared it would "ignore any FKF decisions and threats which violate the previous FIFA and FKF-KPL cooperation agreements and arrangements over the last decade, adding that it would "refocus KPL's limited resources on continuing to make the KPL one of the most corruption-free, professionally managed, highly competitive and widely admired leagues in Africa" instead of "wasting any more time and energy on unproductive wrangles".{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-forges-on-ignores-fkf-directives |title=KPL forges on, ignores FKF directives |date=3 February 2015 |author=Mercy Njueh |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221122806/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-forges-on-ignores-fkf-directives |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} In the FIFA report that was finally sent to KPL chairman Ambrose Rachier, it emerged that FIFA had recommended that the KPL continue to be competed by 16 teams for the 2015 season and that the KPL remain the official body to run the Kenyan top flight on behalf of the FKF.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fifa-report-reveals16-team-league-recommended |title=FIFA Report Reveals;16-team league recommended |date=5 February 2015 |author=Vincent Opiyo |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221122915/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fifa-report-reveals16-team-league-recommended |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} The report also revealed that FKF chairman Sam Nyamweya influenced the promotion of [[Shabana F.C.|Shabana]] from the [[Kenyan National Super League|National Super League]] to the Premier League, a move that was previously questioned by the KPL Governing Council in December 2014.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fifa-report-reveals-nyamweyas-hand-in-shabana-promotion |title=FIFA Report reveals Nyamweya's hand in Shabana promotion |date=5 February 2015 |author=Vincent Opiyo |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221072214/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fifa-report-reveals-nyamweyas-hand-in-shabana-promotion |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-gc-questions-shabana-promotion |title=KPL GC questions Shabana promotion |date=19 December 2014 |author=Dan Ngulu |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221123633/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-gc-questions-shabana-promotion |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} After 2014 league champions [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]] beat 2014 cup champions [[Sofapaka F.C.|Sofapaka]] at the [[2015 Kenyan Super Cup]], the FKF fined both teams a total of KSh.200,000/= each for participating in the unsanctioned match, adding that the teams would face further disciplinary action if they continued to defy them, while the match officials were all also handed three-month bans for participating in the match.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/dstv-super-cup-fkf-distances-itself-promises-sanctions |title=DStv Super Cup: FKF distances itself, promises sanctions |date=10 February 2015 |author=Wilson Mathu |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221022315/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/dstv-super-cup-fkf-distances-itself-promises-sanctions |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-ke/news/4523/kenya-premier-league/2015/02/12/8861032/fkf-fines-gor-mahia-and-sofapaka-bans-referees |title=FKF fines Gor Mahia and Sofapaka, bans referees |date=12 February 2015 |author=Dennis Mabuka |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015}} On 13 February, Sofapaka president Elly Kalekwa announced that neither his club nor any other KPL club would honour the FKF Premier League and pledged to remain a part of the KPL.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-clubs-to-snub-fkfs-league |title=KPL clubs to snub FKF's league |date=13 February 2015 |author=Kevin Teya |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221010800/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-clubs-to-snub-fkfs-league |archive-date=21 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} The FKF later kicked out all KPL clubs from the FKF Premier League and drew member clubs from the National Super League, with its first match ending in a 1–0 victory for [[Shabana F.C.|Shabana]] over [[Nakumatt F.C.|Nakumatt]].{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-pl-wk-1-shabana-goes-top-after-beating-nakumatt |title=FKF PL WK 1: Shabana goes top after beating Nakumatt |date=15 February 2015 |author=Wilson Mathu |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150217105840/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkf-pl-wk-1-shabana-goes-top-after-beating-nakumatt |archive-date=17 February 2015 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-ke/news/4523/kenya-premier-league/2015/02/19/9078642/fkf-promotes-super-league-sides-to-premier-league |title=FKF promotes Super League sides to Premier League |date=19 February 2015 |author=Otieno Otieno |publisher=Goal.com |access-date=21 February 2015}} Having been given until 18 February by Cabinet Secretary Wario to reach an agreement over the running and composition of Kenya's top flight, talks between the KPL and the FKF collapsed once more, with KPL chairman Rachier stating that the KPL walked out on the meeting because the FKF showed up with 30 representatives to outnumber them and win a vote that was to be taken on the issue.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-fkf-talks-collapse |title=KPL, FKF talks collapse |date=18 February 2015 |author=Kevin Teya |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=21 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150220235417/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-fkf-talks-collapse |archive-date=20 February 2015 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }} On 24 February, a court order acquired by the FKF forced the season to be put on hold, while the KPL presented documents challenging the ruling the following day.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kplfkf-feud-kpl-matches-halted |title=KPL/FKF feud: KPL matches halted |date=24 February 2015 |author=Dan Ngulu |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=25 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150224221950/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kplfkf-feud-kpl-matches-halted |archive-date=24 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} After the court injunction was extended in a hearing on 5 March, the [[High Court of Kenya]] allowed the league to continue operations through a ruling delivered on 16 March.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkfkpl-feud-court-extends-injunction |title=FKF/KPL Feud: Court extends injunction |date=5 March 2015 |author=Vincent Opiyo |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=18 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150325151448/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkfkpl-feud-court-extends-injunction |archive-date=25 March 2015 |url-status=dead }} Lady Justice Aburili, who presided over the case, ruled that the FKF could not sue or be sued under its own name unless its officials began legal proceedings on its behalf and advised that a solution to the crisis be agreed on between the two parties out of court.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-can-now-resume-after-court-lifts-injunction |title=KPL can now resume after court lifts injunction |date=16 March 2015 |author=Kevin Teya |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=18 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150318001423/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/kpl-can-now-resume-after-court-lifts-injunction |archive-date=18 March 2015 |url-status=dead }} On 23 March, a FIFA delegation assigned to the case, led by [[Ghana Football Association]] president [[Kwesi Nyantakyi]], announced its support for the 16-team Kenyan Premier League but suggested that the league be contested by 18 teams from 2016 onwards.{{cite web |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkfkpl-feud-fifa-delegation-stands-by-16--team-league |title=FKF/KPL Feud: FIFA delegation stands by 16 - team league |date=23 March 2015 |author=Vincent Opiyo |publisher=Futaa.com |access-date=30 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402183124/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/fkfkpl-feud-fifa-delegation-stands-by-16--team-league |archive-date=2 April 2015 |url-status=dead }} The same day, an agreement was finalised between FKF and KPL representatives, with the two parties agreeing on a number of issues, including the official recognition of the KPL as the top tier and the FKF PL as the second tier of the [[Kenyan football league system]] for 2015 and the allocation of all commercial rights for the top division beginning 2016, as well as a [[memorandum of understanding]] outlining the [[promotion and relegation]] system between the two leagues for 2015 and the relationship between the two parties regarding the government of the top tier beginning 2016.{{cite web |url=http://nairobinews.nation.co.ke/10-things-you-need-to-know-about-fkf-kpl-premier-league-deal/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211022094533/https://nairobinews.nation.co.ke/10-things-you-need-to-know-about-fkf-kpl-premier-league-deal/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 22, 2021 Journalists' Association of Kenya (SJAK), in partnership with the league's sponsors SportPesa, launched the KPL Player of the Month award to be given to the best performing player over each month,
